title: The 8 Levels of Salary & Career Status
house: A bustling metropolitan city where fruit and vegetable people commute on the central subway line, grab morning coffee at the corner kiosk, and hide their glowing forehead salary badges under raincoats.
catchphrase: The glowing number on your forehead never lies.
links: Level 1 mentions a quiet regular at the morning kiosk who always pays with crisp hundred-dollar bills (Level 8).
Level 2's barista remembers a stressed accountant who dropped his briefcase near the subway stairs (Level 3).
Level 3 shares an office floor with a smug marketing director who constantly checks her watch (Level 5).
Level 4 spots a delivery van driven by a guy who only listens to financial podcasts (Level 2).
Level 5 complains about a junior coder who keeps eating all the free breakroom snacks (Level 1).
Level 6 notices a flashy sports car speeding past the bakery every single morning (Level 7).
Level 7 buys her expensive espresso from the very barista who used to work double shifts (Level 2).
Level 8 is the quiet investor who funds the whole district and watches everyone from the penthouse.

levels.open_loop: Who slipped the mysterious fifty-dollar bill into the tip jar while my back was turned?

gegenspieler.tat: Snaps his fingers at her to hurry up with his order and complains that the coffee is too weak.

levels.name: Leo, 22, Dishwasher
levels.story: The 8 Levels of Salary and Career Status. Level 1. Level 1: 1,150 dollars a month, and rent is due tomorrow. My lemon skin feels tight from the steam of the industrial sink. My hands are pruned. I scrub the same greasy pan for the third time because the kitchen manager said you missed a spot. You're barely surviving kid. That stung. I check my mobile banking app for the fourth time today. Zero change. Just then, my phone lights up with a push notification from my landlord. He wants the cash by midnight or I am out on the street. I freeze, staring at the glowing number on my forehead in the greasy mirror above the sink. Then someone leaves a massive tip on the counter outside. You'll see that in Level 2.

levels.name: Mia, 26, Barista
levels.story: Level 2. Level 2: 2,400 dollars a month, and my tip jar is my only safety net. My strawberry seeds ache from standing twelve hours behind the espresso machine. The rent went up again. My roommate texts me asking if I can cover her share of the electricity bill. I massage my temples and force a smile for the next customer in line. You're always so cheerful, how do you do it? A regular asks while tapping his expensive watch impatiently. I look at him, then down at my glowing forehead badge reflecting in the stainless steel milk pitcher. My phone buzzes with a bank alert. An unexpected direct deposit hits my account from an unknown sender. You'll see that in Level 3.

levels.name: Arthur, 34, Junior Accountant
levels.story: Level 3. Level 3: 4,500 dollars a month, and I am drowning in student loans and insurance premiums. My avocado skin is pale from staring at Excel sheets under flickering fluorescent office lights. I check my retirement fund projection and feel a knot in my stomach. Thirty more years of this desk. My boss walks past my cubicle, drops a massive stack of tax files on my keyboard without looking up. Work harder if you ever want a real office, Arthur. That cold whisper cuts deep. I adjust my glasses and stare at the glowing number on my forehead, wishing it would magically double. Suddenly, my office phone rings with an emergency call from corporate auditing. You'll see that in Level 4.

levels.name: Benny, 29, Courier
levels.story: Level 4. Level 4: 6,800 dollars a month from non-stop overtime driving cargo across the city. My orange peel skin is weathered from wind, smog, and endless highway miles. My back aches every time I lift another heavy wooden crate. People think delivery is easy money until they carry a piano up four flights of stairs. You're late with this shipment again, Benny. The client yells, pointing at his wristwatch with an angry expression. I bite my tongue, swallow my pride, and tap my glowing forehead badge to prove my delivery status. My GPS suddenly reroutes me to an upscale gated community across town. You'll see that in Level 5.

levels.name: Chloe, 31, Marketing Lead
levels.story: Level 5. Level 5: 11,500 dollars a month, and my life is ruled by quarterly targets and endless stakeholder meetings. My broccoli crown is perfectly trimmed, but inside I am buzzing with pure anxiety. I own a sleek downtown condo, yet I haven't eaten a home-cooked meal in three weeks. You care more about slide decks than actual people, Chloe. My creative director sighs during the strategy review. That sentence hits me harder than any performance review ever could. I look down at my polished conference table, watching my glowing forehead badge reflect off the glass. My laptop screen suddenly flashes a high-priority calendar invite from the executive suite. You'll see that in Level 6.

levels.name: Derek, 38, Senior Architect
levels.story: Level 6. Level 6: 19,000 dollars a month, and my custom-built architectural firm is the talk of the design district. My coconut shell is hard, polished, and impenetrable to outside critics. I drive a matte-black luxury coupe and vacation in the Maldives twice a year. People think money buys peace of mind, but my phone never stops ringing with demanding billionaire clients. Your design is too radical, we are dropping your firm. The developer barks over the speakerphone during a tense conference call. That arrogant threat shakes my confidence to the core. I stare at the glowing number on my forehead in my bathroom mirror, wondering if I am just a fraud. My banking app sends a sudden notification about a frozen asset account. You'll see that in Level 7.

levels.name: Elena, 42, Tech Founder
levels.story: Level 7. Level 7: 42,000 dollars a month from my artificial intelligence startup, and I finally control the board. My dragonfruit skin is vibrant pink with exotic green scales, armored against every hostile takeover attempt in the valley. I fly private jets and dine with politicians. Yet, loneliness creeps in when the markets close and the penthouse goes silent. You sold out your original vision just to cash out early, Elena. A former co-founder yells at me during a brutal rooftop confrontation. That accusation stings like salt in an open wound. I sip vintage champagne and watch my glowing forehead badge pulse in the dark window glass. My private assistant hands me a sealed envelope marked confidential. You'll see that in Level 8.

levels.name: Victor, 51, Venture Capitalist
levels.story: Level 8. Level 8: 1.25 million dollars a month, and I own the entire financial ecosystem this city runs on. My golden pineapple crown gleams under the penthouse chandelier, every leaf perfectly symmetrical. I fund the startups, control the venture capital funds, and pull the strings behind every glowing forehead badge in the district. You thought you earned your success independently, but every single one of you worked for my portfolio. I whisper this to the empty boardroom while reviewing the district acquisition files. That absolute truth connects every single story from the dishwasher to the tech founder. I look into the panoramic glass wall, watching the entire city glow beneath my feet. Which topic of our society should we expose in the brand new series next week?
